nodes.label: Outlets

recommendations.recommendation_text: Investigate why the lock-in period is 12 months in CP compared to 6 months in other stations, and reduce it if possible.
If the lock-in period cannot be reduced, explore reducing the rent to make outlets more attractive to franchises.
Introduce a tiered/differential pricing system wherein a higher rent is charged for a shorter (e.g., 2-month) lock-in period and a lower rent is charged for a longer (e.g., 6-month) lock-in period.

summary_takeaways: It is important to be MECE at all stages of this problem
Number of outlets could also be divided into total area, area per outlet and % occupied
Please don't start listing possible options and rather make use of some structure

cases.title: Five Star Hotel
cases.problem_statement: Your client is a 5-star hotel in Mumbai. They have been facing lower profitability. You are required to identify the reasons behind the same.

Issue was with the greater influx of business customers, reducing the per customer revenue earned
In the restaurant side, more customers with Zomato Gold or Dineout discounts were causing lower revenue for the restaurant

reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Reveal the 30:70 vs 50:50 split, but do not explain how corporate contracts cap room pricing until the candidate analyzes room rental revenue.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: Who are the primary customer segments visiting our hotel, and has their mix shifted?

reveal_gate.trigger_condition: Candidate asks about revenue streams and Revenue vs. Cost breakdown.
reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Guide candidate to Room Revenues first.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: Let's start by looking at the revenue side, specifically beginning with Room revenues.

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: Within room revenues, the problem is seen in rental revenue (not room service/related purchases). There has been no change in the number of rooms, occupancy rates remain high, and the listed rent charged per room hasn't reduced.

reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Confirm Root Cause #1 and transition the candidate to the Restaurant branch.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: Recall the change in tourist vs. business customer ratio we discussed earlier—how does that affect the effective room rate collected?

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: The hotel has 2 restaurants—an Asian and a Continental one. Lower profits are in the Continental restaurant, driven by a fall in in-dining revenues. Number of tables, occupancy rates, average order quantity, and average menu prices have not changed.

cases.title: Car Insurance Company
cases.problem_statement: Your client is an insurance company who has been facing a decline in its profits since the past year. Analyze the problem and suggest recommendations.
case_facts_given: The client is facing lower profits in the automobile segment
Variable costs for the client have increased
Higher number of claim payouts over the past year

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: The client provides many types of insurance, but the profit decline is primarily in Automobile Insurance. It operates in India in 3 states (Delhi, Maharashtra & Gujarat), selling via car dealer partnerships at purchase and direct customer renewals. The issue is specific to our client.

reveal_gate.trigger_condition: Candidate asks clarifying questions about insurance product line, geography, sales channels, and industry-wide vs. client-specific scope.
reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Do not reveal whether revenues or costs changed yet.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: Before diving into Profit = Revenue - Cost, what clarifying questions would you ask about the insurance product line and geography?

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: Revenues have remained unchanged, and costs have relatively increased.

reveal_gate.trigger_condition: Candidate splits Profit into Revenues and Costs.
reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Do not mention claims payout until the candidate breaks down Fixed and Variable costs.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: Let's check whether the decline in profit is driven by revenues or costs.

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: Within variable costs, the claims payout cost has increased.

reveal_gate.trigger_condition: Candidate breaks costs into Fixed (Operating) and Variable (Claims Payout, Marketing).
reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Do not reveal whether number of payouts or average payout amount increased until asked.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: What are the major fixed and variable cost components for an auto insurance provider?

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: The number of claim payouts has increased (average amount per payout is unchanged).

reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Prompt the candidate to break down External causes further.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: Could the rise in payouts be driven by internal policy/algorithm changes versus external accident frequency?

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: The young population in our customer base has been driving recklessly, leading to a higher number of accidents and claim payouts.

recommendations.recommendation_text: Change the underwriting/claims algorithm to either set a cap on reimbursable damages or incentivize responsible driving via behaviour-based premiums (lower premiums for safe driving track records and vice-versa).
Diversify the customer portfolio both age-wise and state-wise to reduce concentration risk on the bottom line.

summary_takeaways: External issues could have also been divided as vehicle issues vs driver issues
Please don't start laundry-listing options after reaching number of payouts, rather make use of some structure

In the short term, change their algorithm to either set a cap on reimbursable damages or incentivize responsible driving via behaviour-based premiums (low premiums for safe drivers i.e. driving track record and vice-versa) 2. In the long term, the client should diversify its customers both age wise and state wise so that this doesn't affect their bottom-line too much again in the future.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Good recommendations. Thank You. We can close the case here.

cases.title: Tractor Insurance Provider
cases.problem_statement: Your client is an insurance provider facing a decline in profits. Figure out why and suggest recommendations.
case_facts_given: Client deals with tractor insurance, decline in profits since last year
Market has five players with equal market share; industry-wide issue
Demand for tractors has gone down

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: The client deals exclusively with tractor insurance, operates Pan-India serving rural farming customers, and has faced this profit decline for the past 1 year.

reveal_gate.trigger_condition: Candidate asks about insurance type, timeline, geography, and target customer segment.
reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Do not reveal that tractor purchases have declined yet.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: What kind of insurance does the client provide, and who are its typical customers?

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: There are 4 more players in the industry (5 total), all with equal market share. It is an industry-wide issue. The client does not use agents; instead, it has tie-ups with local banks where farmers avail insurance and other facilities.

reveal_gate.trigger_condition: Candidate asks about competitors, industry-wide scope, and distribution channels.
reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Reveal the bank tie-up channel, but do not mention loan defaults or interest rate hikes yet.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: How does the client distribute its policies, and is this issue specific to our client or industry-wide?

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: Revenues have declined (major revenue is insurance premiums collected from customers).

reveal_gate.trigger_condition: Candidate splits Profit into Revenue and Cost.
reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Wait for candidate to break down Premium Revenue before revealing that # of customers declined.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: Let's check whether the profit decline is driven by revenue or cost.

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: The number of customers has gone down (premium per customer per instalment and frequency of instalments are unchanged), and it is driven by a reduction in demand (not supply capacity).

reveal_gate.trigger_condition: Candidate breaks Premium Revenue into # of Customers, Premium per Instalment, and # of Instalments, then splits # of Customers into Demand vs. Supply.
reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Do not mention tractor sales until the candidate maps the insurance customer journey and identifies 'Need'.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: What are the components of premium revenue, and is the drop in customers a demand or supply issue?

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: Within the insurance customer journey, customer 'Need' for tractor insurance has declined.

reveal_gate.trigger_condition: Candidate maps the insurance customer journey (Need, Awareness, Availability, Accessibility, Affordability, Purchase & Post-Purchase Experience).
reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Let the candidate break down why 'Need' for tractor insurance fell (# of tractors purchased vs % insured).
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: Walk through the customer journey of buying tractor insurance—where in that journey is the drop occurring?

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: The number of tractors purchased has reduced (no supply issues with tractors; it is a tractor demand-side issue).

reveal_gate.trigger_condition: Candidate splits insurance need into Total Tractors Purchased and % Buying Insurance, and checks Demand vs. Supply of tractors.
reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Do not reveal affordability until the candidate applies the customer journey to tractor purchases.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: What drives the fundamental need for tractor insurance policies?

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: In the customer journey for buying a tractor, the 'Affordability' of customers has declined. Farmers generally borrow money from local banks, and while farmer income and tractor prices are unchanged, the bank loan has become costly.

reveal_gate.trigger_condition: Candidate applies the customer journey to tractor purchasing and drills into Affordability (own funds vs. bank loans, income vs. loan cost).
reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Wait for candidate to split loan cost into Tractor Price and Interest Rate before revealing the interest rate hike.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: How do farmers typically finance a tractor purchase, and why might their affordability drop?

extracted_case_facts.fact_text: Because of a bad monsoon last year that hurt farmer revenues, many farmers defaulted on their loans, prompting local banks to increase interest rates on tractor loans.

reveal_gate.trigger_condition: Candidate splits loan cost into Tractor Price and Interest Rates and asks why interest rates increased.
reveal_gate.anti_leak_rule: Confirm the root cause and ask for short-term and long-term recommendations.
reveal_gate.missed_fact_fallback_nudge: What are the components of a tractor loan's cost to the farmer, and why would local banks raise interest rates?

recommendations.recommendation_text: Collaborate with local agricultural cooperatives, associations, and farming communities to organize workshops on risk management and the importance of insurance, and offer discounted premiums for group enrollments.
Develop long-term partnerships with tractor manufacturers and dealerships to offer bundled insurance packages at the point of tractor purchase.

summary_takeaways: This is a tough case because the problem doesn't lie within the industry in question, but an industry which is directly linked to it. Customer journey framework needs to be applied twice to deep dive into the problem.

These type of cases are generally longer, and it is essential that they are started well, with appropriate preliminary questions to understand the context well. The recommendations also encourage the interviewee to think out of the box, since very less information is available.
